blocks.text: This chapter follows the message through several stages: Jeremiah dictates it, Baruch writes it and reads it publicly, officials hear and report it, the king has it read and destroys it, and Baruch writes a replacement scroll with additional material. The account also shifts among divine speech, Jeremiah's words, Baruch's scribal work, narration, and the speech of officials and king. These changing voices make the chapter a narrative about both the warning itself and the different ways people receive it.

sections.title: A Written Message Heard by Many Voices

blocks.text: The received book of Jeremiah contains varied forms of writing, including poetry, prose sermons, narratives, letters, headings, repeated accounts, restoration collections, oracles concerning nations, and an appendix. Its present form reflects a long compositional and textual history. A practical outline places chapter 1 at the beginning; chapters 2–25 together; 26–29; 30–33; 34–45; 46–51; and chapter 52 at the close, without deciding how the book was composed.
